problems.title: Squad orders have no screen: the largest measured skill lever in a raid cannot be used
problems.evidence: Logic and tests exist (/home/user/ninja-version-of-game-1/src/gameplay/control/squadPlan.ts; battleSession.ts:105-121; tests/gameplay/control/squad.test.ts passes), but a search of src/presentation and src/app.ts for orderSquad, holdSquad, squadWaiting or SquadOrder finds nothing, and no ui.json key exists. My run (scratch bnl/squad.mjs, raid-bot army, 3 bases per Keep, 9 orders x 6 entry points = 324 raids): Keep 9 bot plan 60.0%, best order and point 100.0%, worst 29.3%; Keep 12 bot plan 49.7%, best 93.3%, worst 22.0%; no planned warrior failed to deploy. The best order differs by base (together+tanks, file+rush, together+rush).
problems.whyItMatters: Formation, wave order and entry point move the same army across a 70-point range, which is the mastery depth the owner asks for, and today only a player who hand-places every warrior can reach it. It needs no rules, save, protocol or server change.
problems.proposedFix: In /home/user/ninja-version-of-game-1/src/presentation/ui/battleHud.ts add a formation picker and a wave-order picker (three choices each, remembered in a device preference), a 'send squad' mode where a tap on an Infiltration Point calls session.orderSquad({point, formation, order}) (wire the point tap in src/presentation/render/BattleScene.ts), and a Hold button with the count while session.squadWaiting > 0. About 11 new keys (squad.*) in locales/en/ui.json, then i18n:sync and 49 translations. Hand placement stays. Measure with Playwright at 320x568, 360x640, 390x844 and 844x390.

problems.title: Warrior Mastery pays +10% HP and damage after one raid and its bonus is in no budget, gate or matchmaking number
problems.evidence: /home/user/ninja-version-of-game-1/src/gameplay/data/progression.json mastery = xpBase 50, xpGrowth 1.35, maxBonus 0.3, xpPerHousingUsed 1, xpPerStar 2. Level 5 (+10.2%) needs 498 EXP; one three-star raid with 120 housing of one type pays 840. Raids to +10% / +15% / +20% / +25% with a one-type army: Keep 4: 1/3/12/126; Keep 12: 1/1/5/48; with five types at Keep 12: 2/5/22/239 (bnl/mastery.mjs). Effect on the raid-bot army, 12 bases, bot plan (bnl/masterypower.mjs): Keep 12 62.8% and 8% three stars at +0%, 73.2% and 25% at +10%, 82.4% and 50% at +17%, 87.4% and 67% at +24%; Keep 15 73.3% to 91.4%; an earlier 18-base run gives +10.7 +- 2.6 points at Keep 12 for +10%. attackerStrength (src/gameplay/sim/matchmaking.ts:126-148) does not read mastery; docs/game-theory/PREVIEW_BALANCE.md has no mastery section.
problems.whyItMatters: Switching features.mastery on as tuned would be a one-evening +15 to +20% power jump for every player followed by a flat curve: it breaks the star-rate gates and gives no long-term chase.
problems.proposedFix: Before any player can earn EXP (the save stores raw EXP): set mastery.xpBase to about 1500 in progression.json (about 40 raids to +10% for a warrior that is a quarter of a Keep 9 army, about 230 to +17%), consider maxBonus 0.30 to 0.15, and either add the bonus to attackerStrength or apply it only against generated bases and Shadow Trials. Add a mastered policy to tools/balance/campaign.ts with a gate, and a mastery table to tools/balance/preview.ts. Ship first as ranks with maxBonus 0 (see opportunities).

problems.title: Hero choice is a false choice: the live Shadow Captain equals or beats every planned hero with that hero's own army
problems.evidence: 18 bases per cell (bnl/heroes.out, tools/balance/preview.ts runHeroPreview with 6 layouts x 3 seeds), hero minus Captain with the hero's own family army: Iron Matriarch +0.3, -3.2, -2.1 (Keeps 9, 12, 15); Sky Admiral -9.7, -5.9, -2.1 (Keeps 11, 13, 15), and only +0.3, +1.0, +0.9 over no hero at all; Grand Sensei -4.4, -6.7, -5.1 (Keeps 13, 14, 15). The Captain is equal or better in 14 of 18 cells. Deploying the hero last does not change it (bnl/herolast.out, 12 bases: Sky Admiral Keep 11 20.5 first, 20.1 last, Captain 28.8 and 26.7). The committed report shows the same sign on 6 bases (docs/game-theory/PREVIEW_BALANCE.md:155-172). Cause read in code: Rally re-arms on every new target (src/gameplay/sim/battle/warriors.ts:304) while the new abilities fire once (heroAbilities.ts:32-34); Sky Admiral tops out at 3,558 HP against the Captain's 9,110.
problems.whyItMatters: A Hero Hall that offers three worse heroes is a trap, not depth. Heroes are the second-best replay lever here only if each one changes how its army plays.
problems.proposedFix: Settle the open Rally question first (docs/game-theory/REQUESTS.md:7), because it sets the baseline. Then retune the three kits in /home/user/ninja-version-of-game-1/src/gameplay/data/planned.json against a written gate (own-family army beats the Captain by 5 or more points at the hero's three Keeps on 30 or more bases; raid mix within 3): for example sky_admiral hpPerHousing 10 to about 22, squall strength 0.5 to 0.7 and durationTicks 50 to 100 and covering flyers deployed during it; bulwark durationTicks 60 to 120. Add the gate as a slow test under tests/gameplay/planned/. Going live after that needs rules:snapshot and SIM_RULES 8.

problems.title: Ten of the fifteen planned counters change nothing in a raid
problems.evidence: 12 bases per cell, three Keeps each, effect = with the building minus with its body only (bnl/countersA.out, countersB.out): Ink Seal Post and Moonlit Gravel 0.0 in all 9 cells but one (+0.3); Spotter's Perch, Listening Jars, Discipline Banner, Rain Barrel Tower (its effect), Straw Scarecrow, Rolling Log Chute, Sand Bucket Post and Sleep Dart Tower within +-1.6 in at least 8 of 9 cells. Working: Steam Vent -5.0, 0.0, -6.6 against its targets; Lightning Rod -6.7, -2.2, -1.2; Whirling Blade Tower -9.2, -4.8, -0.3 but -17.3 and -10.4 against the armies meant to beat it; Mirror Screen -2.9, -2.8, +0.2; Living Bamboo Wall up to -6.3. An independent 18-base run at Keep 15 gives 0.0 +- 0.0 for six of them (bnl/counters15.out). One extra body moves a raid more than most rules: Discipline Banner body at Keep 15 -13.9 points with a 0.0 effect.
problems.whyItMatters: Making all fifteen live would add fifteen bodies to every generated base, shift every balance gate, and give players ten buildings whose translated descriptions promise an effect that does not happen.
problems.proposedFix: Plan a first wave of at most five (steam_vent, lightning_rod_pagoda, whirling_blade_tower with its counteredBy list corrected, mirror_screen at hpMult 1, living_bamboo_wall) and keep the rest not live until their numbers in progression.json buildingCatalog and planned.json pass an acceptance line (effect of -3 or better against the 'it beats' army at two of three Keeps on 24 or more bases), for example sleep seconds 2 to 5, moonlit_gravel radius 0.5 to 2 with a wider troops list. Each live building needs rules:snapshot, SIM_RULES 8, callout labels, a painter, and every balance run.

problems.title: The planned buildings are priced past the whole live defence budget
problems.evidence: bnl/caps.mjs over withPreview data: all sixteen planned buildings to max at Keep 15 cost 616 M Coins and 494 builder-days; every live defence, trap, support and wall together costs 418 M and 407. The five counters that work cost 393 M and 214 builder-days alone (Lightning Rod 154 M; Living Bamboo Wall 3.79 M x 25). Ink Seal Post level 1 is 1.62 M Coins and 7 days; Lightning Rod level 1 is 4.28 M and 7 days. /home/user/ninja-version-of-game-1/src/gameplay/sim/plannedContent.ts:89-91 grows levels past the reference's top by x1.16 power and x1.45 cost, so a level 12 Living Bamboo Wall has 54,761 HP (1.81x a level 13 Stone Wall) for 1,191,459 Coins (8.8x) where planned.json:22 says Stone Wall HP at double the price, and a level 10 Mirror Screen has 125,810 HP (2.3x a max Kunai Tower).
problems.whyItMatters: Live as derived, they would more than double the endgame's defensive grind in one release and put week-long first levels in front of new unlocks, with no campaign run behind it.
problems.proposedFix: In plannedContent.ts previewLevels stop extrapolating past the reference's last level (or lower pinnacleMaxLevel for those entries in progression.json), cap a first level's buildSeconds at one day, and set costMult per building so a first wave adds no more than about 25% to the 418 M and 407-day total; correct the planned.json comments; add a test under tests/gameplay/planned/ that pins the wave's total cost and time. Re-run balance:campaign when any goes live.

problems.title: Shared replays accept an unchecked setup.mastery today, although mastery is not live
problems.evidence: /home/user/ninja-version-of-game-1/server/core/sharedReplays.ts:74 lists 'mastery' in SETUP_KEYS, :118 copies it from the request, :127 re-simulates it with no range check, no features.mastery test and no comparison with the recorded attack; the live engine multiplies HP and damage by 1 + mastery (src/gameplay/sim/battle/battle.ts:293-294). Validate setup.hero against the engine's battle.heroes and level range the same way. Add a case to the shared-replay server tests.

geniusElements.title: withPreview isolation of planned content
geniusElements.whyKeep: The shipped data never contains planned content, and every new hook is reached only when a base holds a planned kind, so live battles, replays, the server and the gates run the same arithmetic. tests/gameplay/planned/progression.test.ts proves a live battle plays the same under both data sets. It is the right pattern for every future feature.

geniusElements.title: Level tables derived from a live reference building or warrior
geniusElements.where: /home/user/ninja-version-of-game-1/src/gameplay/data/planned.json (ref, hpMult, damageMult, costMult); previewLevels and previewHeroDef in plannedContent.ts
geniusElements.whyKeep: One rule instead of hand-typed tables: a planned building or hero follows the live curve automatically, and the hero rule reproduces the Shadow Captain exactly (tested). Only its extrapolation past the reference's top level needs a cap.

geniusElements.title: Squad orders as pure planning that emits ordinary deployments
geniusElements.whyKeep: A formation and wave order become normal deploy calls on their ticks, so records, replays and the server check need no change at all. It adds a large skill lever with zero protocol or rules surface.

geniusElements.title: Body-versus-effect measurement
geniusElements.whyKeep: Fighting each base three ways (without the building, with it, with its body only) separates what a rule does from what extra HP does. It is what exposed the ten no-op counters. Keep the method; raise the sample.

geniusElements.title: Archived battle rules and the snapshot-before-bump order
geniusElements.where: /home/user/ninja-version-of-game-1/server/rules/ (vN, manifest.json digests, archive.ts); tools/release/rules-snapshot.mjs; SIM_RULES_COMPATIBLE in src/gameplay/sim/battle/battle.ts:55
geniusElements.whyKeep: Old clients are checked with their own rules, old replays stay watchable, and a digest test stops an archive from drifting. This is what makes switching content on safe; every go-live step above relies on it.

geniusElements.title: Tempering with rival clans that answer the player's recent raids
geniusElements.where: /home/user/ninja-version-of-game-1/src/gameplay/sim/battle/temper.ts; battle.json temper (offers: recentRaids 10, counterShare 0.5); HUD panel in src/presentation/ui/hud.ts:1616
geniusElements.whyKeep: A fixed-budget reshaping of existing towers, shown at scouting, with an untempered base playing exactly as rules 5. It is the realized core of the Living Fortress design: the best army depends on the base and on the player's own history.

geniusElements.title: Mastery's guard rails
geniusElements.whyKeep: A setup can never claim more than the village earned, donated warriors and the hero earn nothing, and the bonus approaches a cap so numbers stay bounded. The shape is right; only the EXP scale is wrong.

geniusElements.title: The balance lab's method and candour
geniusElements.whyKeep: It tunes to a role frontier, searches for armies that beat the tuning, and reports the pass marks it fails and the limits of its evidence. Keep the lab and its tests as the acceptance method even though its Rules 10 numbers should not ship.

opportunities.where: /home/user/ninja-version-of-game-1/src/gameplay/data/progression.json (mastery); src/gameplay/sim/data.ts (add features); src/presentation/ui/contentPreviewUi.ts masterySection; raid_end event in src/gameplay/sim/village.ts

opportunities.title: Garrison crew: defence and trap builds do not take a Village Artisan

opportunities.description: The hook exists (raids.defenseWin.perStar): a raid held to two stars pays a third of the hold reward, to one star two thirds. Each defence upgrade is felt on the next raid instead of only when a raid is held outright.

opportunities.title: A saved opening per army preset
opportunities.description: After the squad-order screen exists, remember a formation and wave order with each saved army (device preference keyed by preset, no save-format change) and offer it as the default when that army raids.
opportunities.expectedEffect: Players build and refine named plans (army plus opening), which is the loop that keeps strategy players experimenting.

opportunities.title: Building mastery as the defender's counterpart
opportunities.description: progression.json already holds buildingMastery numbers (xpBase 100, maxBonus 0.15) with no simulation behind them. Defences that earn EXP by defending would balance warrior mastery in player-versus-player raids and reward keeping a base.
opportunities.expectedEffect: A long-term reason to care about the home base. Should be a precondition for ever shipping the warrior mastery stat bonus against real players.

opportunities.title: A go-live gate for planned content
opportunities.description: Make the preview a test: a planned counter or hero may be marked live only if a slow test shows its effect on 30 bases (counter: -3 or better against its targets at two of three Keeps; hero: +5 over the Captain with its own family).
opportunities.where: /home/user/ninja-version-of-game-1/tools/balance/preview.ts; a new slow test under tests/gameplay/planned/
opportunities.expectedEffect: No more content that works in unit tests and does nothing in a raid; every future switch-on carries its own evidence.

summary: Only one built-but-not-live system is ready to switch on: squad orders, which have logic and tests but no screen. In 324 measured raids the same army scored between 22% and 100% depending on formation, wave order and entry point (bot plan 60.0% at Keep 9 and 49.7% at Keep 12), and a screen touches only presentation code and translations. The rest is well isolated (the shipped data never holds it; 59 planned-content and squad tests pass) but not ready. Warrior Mastery as tuned pays +10% HP and damage after one raid and lifts Keep 12 three-star rates from 8% to 50% at +17%. No planned hero beats the live Shadow Captain with its own army on 18 bases per cell (Sky Admiral -9.7, -5.9, -2.1). Ten of the fifteen counters change nothing in a raid on 12 bases per cell. The sixteen planned buildings cost 616 M Coins and 494 builder-days to max against 418 M and 407 for every live defensive building. The server would refuse a chosen hero and ignores mastery, the mastery curve sits outside the data version and balance bundles, and shared replays already accept an unchecked mastery field. Rules 10's combat hooks fail their own pass marks and should stay off; its two economy hooks (garrison crew, per-star defence pay) are worth a campaign run. Names and descriptions for all planned content are already translated in every language, but several sentences do not match the code. The three changes I would make first: (1) build the squad-order screen; (2) make the live hero visible and his text true (Rally callout, Keep 7 moment, Codex card) and close the shared-replay mastery hole; (3) retune the mastery curve (xpBase 50 to about 1500) and ship mastery as ranks with no stat bonus, leaving stat bonuses, heroes and a re-priced first wave of five counters for a later rules bump with the server work done.
